question: Assume today is 2026-08-25. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births in Japan in July 2026, as first reported in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (which also count foreign nationals in Japan).

target.what: Number of live births occurring in Japan during July 2026, as counted in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (人口動態統計速報), which includes foreign nationals residing in Japan
target.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (厚生労働省), preliminary monthly vital statistics (人口動態統計速報)
target.cadence: monthly, typically published roughly two months after the reference month (e.g., July data around late September)
target.caveats: The July 2026 preliminary figure would not yet be published as of the 2026-08-25 cutoff, so the target is a future/not-yet-reported value. Definitional notes: preliminary monthly vital statistics count births occurring in Japan to residents and non-residents (including foreign nationals), based on b

candidates.data_to_find: Monthly preliminary birth counts for July in each year 2019-2025 (and ideally all months 2023-2025 to establish seasonality and trend). Minimum: July 2023, 2024, 2025 preliminary birth counts.

assessment.note: Same May 2026 preliminary release: May 2026 births 59,663 vs May 2025 60,718, a 1.7% decline. These are duplicate renderings of one measurement, not independent confirmations.
Same release: Jan-May 2026 cumulative 282,222 vs 280,979 in 2025, +0.4%. Duplicates of one figure.
Trailing 12 months Jun2025-May2026 = 707,052 vs 709,893 prior year, -0.4%. Same underlying release.
July 2025 births 60,650 vs July 2024 62,306, -2.7%. Two vintages of the same July figures agree exactly, so the July 2025 level is well established.
Jan-Jul 2025 cumulative 379,729 vs 392,304 in 2024, -3.2%; consistent with the monthly July figures and the Jan-May cumulative.
Jan 2026 58,694 (+0.5%), Feb 2026 50,761 (-0.4%), Jan-Feb cumulative 109,455 (+0.1%). Consistent with the Jan-May cumulative being roughly flat versus 2025.
Monthly 2026 values (Jan 58,694, Feb 50,761, May 59,663) are consistent with the Jan-May cumulative 282,222; the 2026 year is running close to 2025 levels, unlike the steep 2024-25 declines.
Japanese-national births 2025 = 671,236 (-2.2%); all-person 2025 preliminary = 705,809. The gap (~34,600) is the foreign-national contribution, consistent with the all-person scope of the target.
TFR 2025 = 1.14 vs 2024 = 1.15, well below IPSS medium (1.25) and near low variant (1.10); consistent with continued but slowing decline.
2025 births fell less in major cities (-0.7%) than elsewhere (-2.8%); urban/rural divergence, not a contradiction.

Pregnancy-notification data and conception-to-birth lag (~38 weeks) are internally consistent; but they are 2020-21 vintage and cannot be transferred to Oct 2025 conceptions without a large, unsupported adjustment.
March 2025 and Q1 2025 figures show the steep 2024-25 decline phase; consistent with the July 2025 -2.7% and Jan-Jul -3.2%.

These 2025 mid-year reports (Jan-Jun 2025 ~339,280 or 319,079 excluding foreigners; full-year 2025 ~686,000) are inconsistent with the later official preliminary figures (Jan-May 2026 cumulative 282,222 implies 2025 Jan-May 280,979; full-year 2025 all-person 705,809). They appear to be earlier/partial vintages or different definitions and should not be used as levels.
Oct 2025 59,979 vs Oct 2024 60,213 (-0.4%); Jan-Oct 2025 556,091 vs 571,274 (-2.7%). Consistent with the slowing decline in late 2025.

Marriage counts: May 2026 41,169 (-4.8%), Jan-May 2026 206,971 (+0.4%), trailing 12m 506,485 (+3.2%). Mixed but broadly stable; marriages are a weak, lagged predictor of births and not directly usable for July 2026.
Prefecture-table national totals equal the headline totals (59,663 May; 282,222 Jan-May), confirming internal consistency of the release.
Annualized birth rates (5.7-5.8 per 1,000) are consistent with the monthly counts and population; useful only as a cross-check, not a separate route.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 year-on-year change factor (all-person births)
assumptions.rationale: 2026 has flattened: Jan-May cumulative +0.4% (p5/p6), trailing-12m -0.4% (p8/p9), May -1.7% (p1/p2), Jan-Feb +0.1% (p60/p61). July 2025 itself was -2.7% (p19). A near-flat factor with a wide band centred slightly below 1 reflects the recent easing of decline and the risk of a renewed dip.
assumptions.applies_when: The recent flattening in the Jan-May and trailing-12m cumulative series persists into July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary figure showing a renewed decline of 2%+ year-on-year.

assumptions.name: July share of annual all-person births
assumptions.rationale: July is a high-birth month. From the monthly table, July 2025 60,650 against a 2025 annual all-person total of ~705,809 (p65) gives ~8.6%; July 2024 62,306 against ~686,000 gives ~9.1%. The share is stable, so a band around 8.6% is justified.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 annual total is close to 2025's and the July seasonal share is stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: A 2026 annual total far from 2025's, or evidence of a shifted seasonal pattern.

assumptions.name: 2026 annual all-person births as a factor of 2025
assumptions.rationale: 2025 all-person births were 705,809 (p65). The 2026 year-to-date series is roughly flat (Jan-May +0.4%, trailing-12m -0.4%), so a near-flat annual factor is appropriate, with a band allowing a modest renewed decline.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 annual total tracks the flat year-to-date trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sharp acceleration of decline in mid-2026 monthly data.

methods.label: m1

p16.role: July 2025 all-person live births in Japan (preliminary monthly vital statistics)

a1.role: year-on-year change factor for July 2026 vs July 2025

methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 route: July 2025 level (p16) times a year-on-year change factor. The factor is now anchored on the 2026 flattening (Jan-May +0.4%, trailing-12m -0.4%) rather than a generic decline. Shared dependency: p16 is the same source family as the target; failure mode is a renewed steep decline in mid-2026.

methods.label: m2

p65.role: 2025 all-person live births in Japan (preliminary annual total)

a3.role: 2026 annual all-person births as a factor of 2025

a2.role: July share of annual all-person births

methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 annual-times-share route, now with an explicit 2026 annual factor (a3) instead of assuming the 2025 level. p65 is the all-person annual total matching the target definition. Failure modes: the annual factor and the July share are both uncertain; the July share is derived from the same source family.

weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p118: October 2025 figure is for Japanese residents only, not the all-person (including foreign nationals) target quantity.; p119: October 2024 figure is described as provisional comparison-year data without the all-person definition, so it does not match the target quantity's entity/measure.

kept.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 year-on-year change factor (all-person births)
kept.rationale: 2026 has flattened: Jan-May cumulative +0.4% (p5/p6), trailing-12m -0.4% (p8/p9), May -1.7% (p1/p2), Jan-Feb +0.1% (p60/p61). July 2025 itself was -2.7% (p19). A near-flat factor with a wide band centred slightly below 1 reflects the recent easing of decline and the risk of a renewed dip.
kept.applies_when: The recent flattening in the Jan-May and trailing-12m cumulative series persists into July 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary figure showing a renewed decline of 2%+ year-on-year.

kept.name: July share of annual all-person births
kept.rationale: July is a high-birth month. From the monthly table, July 2025 60,650 against a 2025 annual all-person total of ~705,809 (p65) gives ~8.6%; July 2024 62,306 against ~686,000 gives ~9.1%. The share is stable, so a band around 8.6% is justified.
kept.applies_when: The 2026 annual total is close to 2025's and the July seasonal share is stable.
kept.falsified_by: A 2026 annual total far from 2025's, or evidence of a shifted seasonal pattern.

kept.name: 2026 annual all-person births as a factor of 2025
kept.rationale: 2025 all-person births were 705,809 (p65). The 2026 year-to-date series is roughly flat (Jan-May +0.4%, trailing-12m -0.4%), so a near-flat annual factor is appropriate, with a band allowing a modest renewed decline.
kept.applies_when: The 2026 annual total tracks the flat year-to-date trend.
kept.falsified_by: A sharp acceleration of decline in mid-2026 monthly data.

Two routes were combined with equal weight per block. m1 ([[m1_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m1_weight]]) scales the observed July 2025 preliminary figure of [[p16_value]] by an assumed near-flat year-on-year factor of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]). m2 ([[m2_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m2_weight]]) multiplies the observed 2025 all-person annual total of [[p65_value]] by an assumed 2026 annual factor of [[a3_value]] and an assumed July share of [[a2_value]]. The observed points are historical; the factors and share are analyst assumptions, not observations.

The main risk is a renewed steep decline in mid-2026, which would push the true value below both routes. The most useful missing evidence would be actual July 2026 monthly counts or a longer, stable monthly series to pin down the July share and the year-on-year factor.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
